body.statement:
Fix \(n\), \(G\), \(r\), and a deterministic returned map \(F_G\), assume that \(\mathcal C_G(\delta_{\mathrm{chart}},\kappa_{\mathrm{chart}},K_{\mathrm{chart}},\nu_{\mathrm{chart}})\neq\varnothing\), and use the total pole and singular-covariance conventions in \(\mathrm{def:plug\mbox{-}in\mbox{-}estimator}\) and \(\mathrm{def:simultaneous\mbox{-}wald\mbox{-}set}\). Uniformly over \(\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G(\delta_{\mathrm{chart}},\kappa_{\mathrm{chart}},K_{\mathrm{chart}},\nu_{\mathrm{chart}})\),
\[
\sqrt N\{\widehat\theta_G-F_G(s)\}=N^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^N\operatorname{IF}_F(X_i)+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,V_F),\qquad \widehat V_F\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}V_F.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}\Pr_{\Sigma}\!\left\{\min_{1\le j\le r}|Q_{F,j}(\operatorname{vech}\widehat\Sigma)|=0\right\}\to0,\qquad \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}\Pr_{\Sigma}\{\widehat V_F\text{ is singular}\}\to0.
\]
Consequently \(\inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}\Pr_{\Sigma}\{F_G(s)\in\mathcal W_{G,N}(1-\gamma)\}\to1-\gamma\). The result covers every fixed finite vector of rational formulas returned by the total schedule on the Gaussian submodel; it makes no efficiency claim.
body.justification: A symbolic inverse becomes empirically usable only after its full joint first-order law and simultaneous coverage are supplied.
body.gap: Mareis, Sturma, and Drton treat fixed half-trek estimators, whereas the returned map here may be any deterministic rational quotient produced by degree-bounded elimination; Drton and Xiao show why the nondegeneracy boundary cannot be ignored.
body.consumer: An analyst can report simultaneous confidence regions for all structural coefficients returned by the exact stopping schedule on a declared regular chart.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(m=n(n+1)/2\), write \(\widehat s=\operatorname{vech}(\widehat\Sigma)\), and abbreviate the nonempty chart in the statement by \(\mathcal C_G\).  All limits below are uniform over \(\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G\): explicitly, \(R_N=o_{\mathbb P}^{\mathcal C_G}(1)\) means that \(\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}\Pr_\Sigma(\lVert R_N\rVert>\epsilon)\to0\) for every \(\epsilon>0\).

First we record the distribution and the uniform moment bounds used below.  By \(\mathrm{ass:linear\mbox{-}sem}\), the unique linear solution is
\[
 X=(I_n-\Lambda^{\mathsf T})^{-1}\varepsilon=(I_n-\Lambda)^{-\mathsf T}\varepsilon.
\]
Consequently, \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\mbox{-}noise}\) and the definition of \(\Sigma\) give
\[
 X\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma).
\tag{1}
\]
The eigenvalue restrictions in \(\mathrm{def:regular\mbox{-}chart}\) place \(\mathcal C_G\) inside
\[
 \mathcal K=\{\Sigma\in\mathbb S^n:\kappa_{\mathrm{chart}}I_n\preceq\Sigma\preceq K_{\mathrm{chart}}I_n\},
\]
which is compact.  On the set where all returned denominators are nonzero, \(F_G\), its derivatives, and the Gaussian moment matrix \(V_F\) are continuous functions of \(s=\operatorname{vech}(\Sigma)\).  Thus the four weak inequalities defining \(\mathcal C_G\) specify a closed subset of \(\mathcal K\), so \(\mathcal C_G\) is compact.  If \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_n)\), then (1) permits the representation \(X\overset{d}=\Sigma^{1/2}Z\), and hence, for every fixed positive integer \(k\),
\[
 \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}\mathbb E_\Sigma\lVert X\rVert^k
 \le K_{\mathrm{chart}}^{k/2}\mathbb E\lVert Z\rVert^k<\infty.
\tag{2}
\]

Define
\[
 Y_i=\operatorname{vech}(X_iX_i^{\mathsf T}-\Sigma).
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:iid\mbox{-}sampling}\), the \(Y_i\) are independent and identically distributed, have mean zero, and have uniformly bounded moments of every fixed order by (2).  The definition of \(\widehat\Sigma\) gives the exact decomposition
\[
 \widehat s-s=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i-operatorname{vech}(\bar X\bar X^{\mathsf T}).
\tag{3}
\]
Coordinatewise Chebyshev bounds, using the uniformly bounded second moments in (2), show that
\[
 \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i=O_{\mathbb P}^{\mathcal C_G}(N^{-1/2}),
 \qquad
 \bar X=O_{\mathbb P}^{\mathcal C_G}(N^{-1/2}).
\]
Because \(m\) and \(n\) are fixed, (3) therefore yields
\[
 \widehat s-s=O_{\mathbb P}^{\mathcal C_G}(N^{-1/2}),
 \qquad
 \sqrt N\operatorname{vech}(\bar X\bar X^{\mathsf T})
 =O_{\mathbb P}^{\mathcal C_G}(N^{-1/2}).
\tag{4}
\]

We next exclude empirical poles uniformly.  The compact set \(\operatorname{vech}(\mathcal C_G)\), continuity of the finitely many polynomials \(Q_{F,j}\), and the chart inequality
\[
 \min_{1\le j\le r}|Q_{F,j}(s)|\ge\delta_{\mathrm{chart}}>0
\]
imply that there is a single \(\eta>0\) such that, for every \(s\in\operatorname{vech}(\mathcal C_G)\),
\[
 \lVert t-s\rVert\le\eta
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \min_{1\le j\le r}|Q_{F,j}(t)|\ge\delta_{\mathrm{chart}}/2.
\tag{5}
\]
The closed \(\eta\)-tube in (5) is compact and contains no pole.  The fixed rational map \(F_G\) consequently has uniformly bounded first and second derivatives there.  Taylor's formula with its second-order remainder, followed by (3)--(5), gives on the event \(\lVert\widehat s-s\rVert\le\eta\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sqrt N\{F_G(\widehat s)-F_G(s)\}
 &=J_F(s)\sqrt N(\widehat s-s)
   +O_{\mathbb P}^{\mathcal C_G}\!\left(\sqrt N\lVert\widehat s-s\rVert^2\right)\\
 &=\frac1{\sqrt N}\sum_{i=1}^N J_F(s)Y_i
   -J_F(s)\sqrt N\operatorname{vech}(\bar X\bar X^{\mathsf T})
   +o_{\mathbb P}^{\mathcal C_G}(1)\\
 &=\frac1{\sqrt N}\sum_{i=1}^N\operatorname{IF}_F(X_i)
   +o_{\mathbb P}^{\mathcal C_G}(1).
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
By (4), the complement of this event has probability tending to zero uniformly.  Equation (5) also shows that the pole convention in \(\mathrm{def:plug\mbox{-}in\mbox{-}estimator}\) is never invoked on the event.  Hence (6) remains true for the total estimator \(\widehat\theta_G\).

For completeness, we establish the required uniform central limit statement directly.  Let
\[
 \psi_\Sigma(X)=\operatorname{IF}_F(X)=J_F(s)\operatorname{vech}(XX^{\mathsf T}-\Sigma),
 \qquad
 Z_\Sigma=V_F(\Sigma)^{-1/2}\psi_\Sigma(X).
\]
The chart condition \(\lambda_{\min}(V_F)\ge\nu_{\mathrm{chart}}>0\), the uniform bound on \(J_F\), and (2) imply
\[
 \mathbb E_\Sigma Z_\Sigma=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_\Sigma Z_\Sigma Z_\Sigma^{\mathsf T}=I_r,
 \qquad
 \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}\mathbb E_\Sigma\lVert Z_\Sigma\rVert^3<\infty.
\tag{7}
\]
Here the middle equality follows from the definition of \(V_F\), and its inverse exists by the displayed chart condition.

Let \(G_1,\ldots,G_N\) be independent \(\mathcal N(0,I_r)\) vectors, independent of the sample.  For a bounded function \(h:\mathbb R^r\to\mathbb R\) with Lipschitz constant at most one, let \(h_\epsilon(x)=\mathbb E\{h(x+\epsilon G_0)\}\), where \(G_0\sim\mathcal N(0,I_r)\).  Gaussian convolution and differentiation under the integral give constants depending only on \(r\) such that
\[
 \lVert h-h_\epsilon\rVert_\infty\le C_r\epsilon,
 \qquad
 \sup_x\lVert D^3h_\epsilon(x)\rVert\le C_r\epsilon^{-2}.
\tag{8}
\]
Replace the summands \(Z_{\Sigma,i}/\sqrt N\) one at a time by \(G_i/\sqrt N\).  Conditional third-order Taylor expansion of \(h_\epsilon\) about the sum of the other terms has identical constant, linear, and quadratic expectations for the two increments by (7).  The integral remainder, (7), and the finite third Gaussian moment therefore imply
\[
 \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}
 \left|\mathbb E_\Sigma h_\epsilon\!\left(N^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^N Z_{\Sigma,i}\right)
 -\mathbb E h_\epsilon\!\left(N^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^N G_i\right)\right|
 \le C_rN^{-1/2}\epsilon^{-2}.
\tag{9}
\]
Since \(N^{-1/2}\sum_iG_i\sim\mathcal N(0,I_r)\), taking \(\epsilon=N^{-1/6}\) in (8)--(9) proves, in bounded-Lipschitz distance,
\[
 \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
 \mathcal L_\Sigma\!\left[V_F(\Sigma)^{-1/2}N^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^N\operatorname{IF}_F(X_i)\right],
 \mathcal N(0,I_r)
 \right)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{10}
\]
Continuity on the compact chart gives \(\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}\lambda_{\max}(V_F)<\infty\).  Thus (10), after multiplication by \(V_F^{1/2}\), is precisely the uniform interpretation of
\[
 N^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^N\operatorname{IF}_F(X_i)
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,V_F).
\tag{11}
\]
Together, (6) and (11) prove the asserted asymptotic linear expansion and Gaussian limit.

It remains to prove consistency of the plug-in covariance.  On the event in (5), put
\[
 \widehat\psi_i
 =J_F(\widehat s)\operatorname{vech}(X_iX_i^{\mathsf T}-\widehat\Sigma),
 \qquad
 \psi_i=J_F(s)Y_i.
\]
For each entry of \(\psi_i\psi_i^{\mathsf T}\), Chebyshev's inequality and (2) with \(k=8\) give the uniform law of large numbers
\[
 \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\psi_i\psi_i^{\mathsf T}-V_F
 =o_{\mathbb P}^{\mathcal C_G}(1).
\tag{12}
\]
The mean-value bound on the tube, (4), and the identity
\[
 \widehat\psi_i-\psi_i
 =\{J_F(\widehat s)-J_F(s)\}Y_i
   -J_F(\widehat s)(\widehat s-s)
\]
show that
\[
 \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\lVert\widehat\psi_i-\psi_i\rVert^2
 =o_{\mathbb P}^{\mathcal C_G}(1),
\tag{13}
\]
because \(N^{-1}\sum_i\lVert Y_i\rVert^2=O_{\mathbb P}^{\mathcal C_G}(1)\).  Applying Cauchy--Schwarz to the difference of the empirical second moments and using (12)--(13) gives
\[
 \widehat V_F-V_F=o_{\mathbb P}^{\mathcal C_G}(1).
\tag{14}
\]
The complement of the tube again has uniformly vanishing probability, so the total convention \(\widehat V_F=0\) at a pole does not change (14).

The two exceptional-event claims now follow.  From (4)--(5),
\[
 \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}
 \Pr_\Sigma\!\left\{\min_j|Q_{F,j}(\widehat s)|=0\right\}
 \le
 \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}\Pr_\Sigma\{\lVert\widehat s-s\rVert>\eta\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{15}
\]
For symmetric matrices, the variational formula for the least eigenvalue gives
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat V_F)
 \ge\lambda_{\min}(V_F)-\lVert\widehat V_F-V_F\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Therefore (14) and \(\lambda_{\min}(V_F)\ge\nu_{\mathrm{chart}}\) imply
\[
 \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}\Pr_\Sigma\{\widehat V_F\text{ is singular}\}
 \le
 \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}
 \Pr_\Sigma\{\lVert\widehat V_F-V_F\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\ge\nu_{\mathrm{chart}}/2\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{16}
\]

On the complement of the events in (15)--(16), (6), (10), and (14) imply
\[
 N\{\widehat\theta_G-F_G(s)\}^{\mathsf T}\widehat V_F^{-1}
 \{\widehat\theta_G-F_G(s)\}\rightsquigarrow\chi_r^2
\tag{17}
\]
uniformly over the chart.  Indeed, the inverse perturbation identity
\[
 \widehat V_F^{-1}-V_F^{-1}
 =\widehat V_F^{-1}(V_F-\widehat V_F)V_F^{-1}
\]
and the common lower eigenvalue bound make the studentization error \(o_{\mathbb P}^{\mathcal C_G}(1)\), while (10) makes the leading quadratic form converge uniformly to the squared norm of a standard \(r\)-variate Gaussian vector.  The \(\chi_r^2\) distribution is continuous at \(\chi^2_{r,1-\gamma}\).  On either exceptional event, \(\mathrm{def:simultaneous\mbox{-}wald\mbox{-}set}\) sets the confidence set equal to \(\mathbb R^r\); those events have uniformly vanishing probability by (15)--(16).  It follows from (17) that
\[
 \inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal C_G}
 \Pr_\Sigma\{F_G(s)\in\mathcal W_{G,N}(1-\gamma)\}
 \longrightarrow1-\gamma.
\tag{18}
\]

Finally, the statistical target in (6)--(18) is the observed-law functional \(F_G(s)\), not a structural coordinate by definition.  When the exact call in \(\mathrm{thm:total\mbox{-}stopping\mbox{-}schedule}\) succeeds, its retained certificate for the coordinate \(q\) represented by the \(j\)-th returned quotient is
\[
 qQ_{F,j}(s)-P_{F,j}(s)\in I_G.
\]
Applying \(\tau_G\), using \(I_G=\ker(\tau_G)\), and using the nonzero-denominator condition (5) at the population covariance yields
\[
 0=qQ_{F,j}(s)-P_{F,j}(s),
 \qquad
 q=\frac{P_{F,j}(s)}{Q_{F,j}(s)}.
\tag{19}
\]
Thus, coordinatewise, \(\theta_G=F_G(\operatorname{vech}\Sigma)\) on the successful graph model and the regular chart.  Equation (19) proves the link by which (18) becomes simultaneous inference for the structural vector; no part of the argument asserts efficiency.
